overview: Both are major biomolecules, but one is built from sugar units and the other from amino acids with a far more complex structure.
genZNote: Carbs: simple sugar chains. Proteins: complex, folded 3D machines.

aspects.label: Building Block (Monomer)
aspects.valueB: Amino acids, joined by peptide bonds.

aspects.label: Elements Present
aspects.valueB: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, and often sulfur.

aspects.label: Primary Biological Role
aspects.valueA: Mainly energy storage and structural support (e.g. cellulose).
aspects.valueB: Mainly structural, enzymatic, and functional roles (e.g. enzymes, antibodies, hormones).

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Nitrogen is present in proteins but absent from carbohydrates — a quick way to distinguish them in a biochemical test question.
overlay.memoryTrick: If nitrogen is in the molecule, think protein, not carbohydrate.
overlay.commonMisconception: Proteins are not primarily used for energy under normal conditions — they're reserved as an energy source only when carbs and fats run low.
